facts.statement: SFO’s BART station is in the International Terminal; the free AirTrain connects airport terminals to the station.
facts.evidence: The BART station is located in the International Terminal

facts.statement: The SFMTA adult single-ride page lists a $2.85 Clipper fare for adults ages 19–64. The same fare table lists contactless credit/debit payment at $2.85; this is not a promise of discounted-program eligibility.
The adult ordinary Muni single-ride fare covers 120 minutes across buses and light rail under SFMTA’s transfer conditions; this does not establish cable-car or other-operator coverage.

SFMTA lists the Muni-Only Day Pass at $5.70 for unlimited Muni buses, trains and historic streetcars through 11:59 p.m. It lists MuniMobile and Clipper pre-purchase, or cash at a vehicle farebox after notifying the operator; cable cars are not included in this listed coverage.

The one-day Visitor Passport fare table lists $15.00 for MuniMobile, Paper Passport and Clipper. The Muni-only product includes cable cars but excludes BART, other transit systems and SFO airport transportation; no channel-specific discount is promised here.
The F Market & Wharves stop list includes the Ferry Building, Pier 39 and Fisherman’s Wharf stops. Opposite directions use different stops; this is not a live-service or step-free-access guarantee.

facts.statement: Golden Gate Transit’s bridge visitor guide describes transit access at the south and north bridge ends. Use current timetables for routes and stops; older route-number examples in the visitor guide are not current-service authority.

facts.statement: Golden Gate Bridge pedestrians, including wheelchair users, are restricted to the east sidewalk. Seasonal hours, dated alerts and temporary closures need checking for the travel date; this is not confirmation of uninterrupted current access.
facts.evidence: Pedestrians - Daily Access on the EAST Sidewalk

sources.title: Tap to Pay with a Contactless Bank Card

facts.statement: For contactless bank-card payment, each rider needs their own card or mobile device. On services requiring both entry and exit taps, use the same card or device for both; this does not mean that every operator requires an exit tap.
facts.evidence: Each rider must pay with their own card or mobile device
